## T1: Agent-to-agent protocols and multi-agent interoperability

### AMN-005

**Announcing the Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)**. Rao Surapaneni, Miku Jha, Michael Vakoc, Todd Segal. *Google Developers Blog*, 2025-04-09. <https://developers.googleblog.com/en/a2a-a-new-era-of-agent-interoperability/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `google2025announcing`.

Google introduced Agent2Agent (A2A), an open protocol for communication between AI agents built by different vendors and on different frameworks, with the draft specification published on GitHub. Google says the launch had backing from more than 50 technology partners plus services firms such as Accenture, Deloitte and KPMG. The post positions A2A as complementary to Anthropic's MCP: MCP supplies tools and context to an agent, while A2A handles agent-to-agent communication.

- **Relevance:** This is the origin event for the dominant open standard for cross-vendor task delegation between agents.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust. **Technologies:** A2A, MCP.
- **Source:** official-blog, primary; claim status: vendor-claim; verified by fetch. Note: Fetched page does not name a license; secondary sources state Apache 2.0.

### AMN-008

**Empowering multi-agent apps with the open Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol**. Yina Arenas, Bas Brekelmans. *Microsoft Cloud Blog*, 2025-05-07. <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-cloud/blog/2025/05/07/empowering-multi-agent-apps-with-the-open-agent2agent-a2a-protocol/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `microsoft2025empowering`.

Microsoft announced that A2A support was coming to Azure AI Foundry and Copilot Studio, with a public preview promised soon but no date given. Microsoft says it joined the A2A working group on GitHub, that agents built with Semantic Kernel or LangChain can interoperate over A2A, and that calls would be protected with Microsoft Entra, mutual TLS, content safety and audit logs. A Semantic Kernel Python sample showed two local agents collaborating.

- **Relevance:** A second hyperscaler adopting a Google-originated protocol was an early signal that A2A could serve as a cross-vendor delegation layer.
- **Operations:** delegation, cross-framework-migration, identity-trust. **Technologies:** A2A, Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio, Semantic Kernel, Microsoft Entra.
- **Source:** official-blog, primary; claim status: vendor-claim; verified by fetch.

### AMN-014

**Linux Foundation Launches the Agent2Agent Protocol Project to Enable Secure, Intelligent Communication Between AI Agents**. Linux Foundation. *Linux Foundation*, 2025-06-23. <https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-launches-the-agent2agent-protocol-project-to-enable-secure-intelligent-communication-between-ai-agents> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `linux2025linux`.

At Open Source Summit North America in Denver on 23 June 2025, the Linux Foundation announced that it would host the Agent2Agent (A2A) project, an agent-to-agent communication protocol that Google created and launched in April, and pointed readers to github.com/a2aproject/A2A. The release says the protocol has support from more than 100 technology companies and includes supporting statements from Google Cloud, AWS, Cisco (Outshift), Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP and ServiceNow. Executive Director Jim Zemlin said joining the foundation gives A2A long-term neutrality, collaboration and governance.

- **Relevance:** Moving A2A to neutral governance reduced single-vendor risk for a protocol meant to carry tasks across organizational boundaries.
- **Operations:** delegation, governance. **Technologies:** A2A.
- **Source:** press-release, primary; claim status: fact; verified by fetch.

### AMN-021

**Linux Foundation Welcomes the AGNTCY Project to Standardize Open Multi-Agent System Infrastructure and Break Down AI Agent Silos**. Linux Foundation. *Linux Foundation*, 2025-07-29. <https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-welcomes-the-agntcy-project-to-standardize-open-multi-agent-system-infrastructure-and-break-down-ai-agent-silos> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `linux2025linuxa`.

Cisco contributed AGNTCY, the 'Internet of Agents' infrastructure project it open-sourced in March 2025 with LangChain and Galileo, to the Linux Foundation. Cisco, Dell Technologies, Google Cloud, Oracle and Red Hat joined as formative members, and the release cites more than 65 supporting companies. Components cover agent discovery via the Open Agent Schema Framework (OASF), cryptographic agent identity, the SLIM messaging layer and multi-agent observability, and the project says it interoperates with A2A and MCP.

- **Relevance:** AGNTCY targets the discovery, identity, messaging and observability layers around A2A, which are needed for accountable agent-to-agent hand-offs.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust, observability. **Technologies:** AGNTCY, OASF, SLIM, A2A, MCP.
- **Source:** press-release, primary; claim status: fact; verified by fetch. Note: Secondary coverage cites more than 75 supporters; the LF release says more than 65.

### AMN-023

**Announcing a complete developer toolkit for scaling A2A agents on Google Cloud**. Rao Surapaneni, Philip Stephens. *Google Cloud Blog*, 2025-08-01. <https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/agent2agent-protocol-is-getting-an-upgrade> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `google2025announcingb`.

Google announced A2A v0.3, adding gRPC support, the ability to sign security cards (agent cards), and extended client support in the Python SDK; it says the ecosystem had grown past 150 organizations. Alongside it, Google added native A2A support in the Agent Development Kit, deployment paths on Agent Engine (announced as coming soon), Cloud Run and GKE, A2A evaluation in Vertex GenAI Evaluation Service, and listing of A2A agents in its AI Agent Marketplace. Partner examples include ServiceNow and Twilio, and community tools such as A2A Inspector and a Technology Compatibility Kit are mentioned.

- **Relevance:** Signed agent cards and transport choice (gRPC) address identity and deployment portability for agents that delegate across hosts.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust, runtime-relocation. **Technologies:** A2A, gRPC, Agent Development Kit, Agent Engine, Cloud Run, GKE.
- **Source:** official-blog, primary; claim status: vendor-claim; verified by fetch. Note: URL slug and HTML title read 'Agent2Agent protocol (A2A) is getting an upgrade'; page heading is as given. Some secondary coverage dates it 2025-07-31; the fetched page shows 2025-08-01.

### AMN-028

**ACP Joins Forces with A2A**. Kate Blair, Todd Segal. *LF AI & Data Foundation*, 2025-08-29. <https://lfaidata.foundation/communityblog/2025/08/29/acp-joins-forces-with-a2a-under-the-linux-foundations-lf-ai-data/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `lf2025acp`.

IBM Research's Agent Communication Protocol (ACP), launched in March 2025 to power the BeeAI platform, is merging into A2A under the Linux Foundation, and the ACP team is ending active development. Kate Blair joins the A2A Technical Steering Committee for IBM, alongside Google, Microsoft, AWS, Cisco, Salesforce, ServiceNow and SAP. BeeAI agents can become A2A-compliant through an A2AServer adapter and consume external A2A agents through an A2AAgent client, and a migration guide is provided.

- **Relevance:** The merger consolidated two competing agent-to-agent protocols and created an explicit protocol-migration path for existing agents.
- **Operations:** delegation, cross-framework-migration, governance. **Technologies:** ACP, A2A, BeeAI.
- **Source:** official-blog, primary; claim status: fact; verified by fetch. Note: Page shows a last-updated date of 2025-09-04.

### AMN-030

**Powering AI commerce with the new Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)**. Stavan Parikh, Rao Surapaneni. *Google Cloud Blog*, 2025-09-16. <https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/announcing-agents-to-payments-ap2-protocol> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `google2025powering`.

Google announced the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), designed as an extension of A2A and usable with MCP, for agent-initiated payments across cards, stablecoins and real-time bank transfers. AP2 relies on cryptographically signed 'mandates' (an Intent Mandate and a Cart Mandate) that serve as verifiable proof of user authorization and form an audit trail. Google says more than 60 organizations collaborated, including American Express, Mastercard, PayPal, Coinbase, Salesforce and ServiceNow, and it also launched an A2A x402 extension for crypto payments with Coinbase, the Ethereum Foundation and MetaMask.

- **Relevance:** AP2's signed mandates are a concrete mechanism for carrying user authority and accountability along with a delegated task.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust, governance. **Technologies:** AP2, A2A, MCP, x402, Verifiable Credentials.
- **Source:** official-blog, primary; claim status: vendor-claim; verified by fetch.

### AMN-038

**Building Trust at Internet Scale: GoDaddy's Agent Name Service Registry for the Agentic AI Marketplace**. Scott Courtney. *GoDaddy*, 2025-10-02. <https://www.godaddy.com/resources/news/building-trust-at-internet-scale-godaddys-agent-name-service-registry-for-the-agentic-ai-marketplace> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `godaddy2025building`.

GoDaddy described an Agent Name Service registry with a registration authority, building on the IETF and OWASP ANS work, so that agents can discover and verify each other. Its trust chain combines customer verification, ACME DNS-01 domain validation, hybrid public/private certificates, DNSSEC-secured records (TXT records pointing to an Agent Card, plus TLSA/DANE pinning) and Merkle-tree transparency logging. GoDaddy said a developer preview would follow in the coming weeks.

- **Relevance:** It is an early commercial attempt to anchor agent identity and agent-card discovery in existing DNS/PKI infrastructure.
- **Operations:** identity-trust, delegation. **Technologies:** Agent Name Service (ANS), DNS, DNSSEC, DANE, PKI, A2A.
- **Source:** official-blog, primary; claim status: vendor-claim; verified by fetch. Note: Author Scott Courtney per page byline and meta author; date 2025-10-02 from page metadata.

### AMN-047

**When AI Agents Go Rogue: Agent Session Smuggling Attack in A2A Systems**. Royce Lu, Jay Chen. *Palo Alto Networks Unit 42*, 2025-10-31. <https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/agent-session-smuggling-in-agent2agent-systems/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `palo2025when`.

Unit 42 described 'agent session smuggling', in which a malicious remote agent exploits the stateful, multi-turn nature of an A2A session to inject covert instructions into a victim client agent. Proof-of-concept attacks built with Google's ADK extracted the client's system instructions, tool schemas and chat history, and triggered an unauthorized stock purchase. The authors say this is not a flaw in A2A itself but a consequence of implicit inter-agent trust, and they report no attacks seen in the wild. Proposed mitigations include out-of-band human approval, context grounding, signed agent cards and exposing agent activity to users.

- **Relevance:** It shows that delegating to a peer agent opens a new trust boundary and needs identity, provenance and audit controls.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust, observability. **Technologies:** A2A, Agent Development Kit.
- **Source:** research-news, primary; claim status: incident; verified by fetch. Note: The 'incident' label refers to a demonstrated attack technique; no exploitation was observed in the wild.

### AMN-049

**Introducing agent-to-agent protocol support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime**. ## T2: Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem

### AMN-001

**Introducing the Model Context Protocol**. Anthropic. *Anthropic*, 2024-11-25. <https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `anthropic2024introducing`.

Anthropic open-sourced the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting AI assistants to data sources such as content repositories, business tools and development environments. The launch included the specification and SDKs on GitHub, local MCP server support in Claude Desktop, and pre-built servers for Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, Git, Postgres and Puppeteer. Anthropic named Block and Apollo as early integrators and said Zed, Replit, Codeium and Sourcegraph were working with MCP.

- **Relevance:** This is the origin event for the agent-to-tool layer that later handoff and migration designs assume as a common substrate.
- **Operations:** tool-access. **Technologies:** MCP, Claude Desktop.

### AMN-003

**MCP Security Notification: Tool Poisoning Attacks**. Luca Beurer-Kellner, Marc Fischer. *Invariant Labs*, 2025-04-01. <https://invariantlabs.ai/blog/mcp-security-notification> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `invariant2025mcp`.

Invariant Labs disclosed Tool Poisoning Attacks, in which malicious instructions hidden in MCP tool descriptions are seen by the model but not the user. In a Cursor experiment, a poisoned 'add' tool made the agent read ~/.cursor/mcp.json and SSH keys and pass them to the attacker's server. The post also described 'rug pulls' (a server changing tool descriptions after approval) and 'tool shadowing' (one server's description hijacking a trusted send_email tool), and recommended tool pinning and cross-server dataflow controls.

- **Relevance:** Shows that tool metadata travelling with an agent is an attack surface, so any portable task context or handoff must treat tool descriptions as untrusted and integrity-pinned.
- **Operations:** tool-access, identity-trust. **Technologies:** MCP, Cursor.
- **Source:** research-news, primary; claim status: incident; verified by fetch.

### AMN-012

David Weston. *Microsoft (Windows Experience Blog)*, 2025-05-19. <https://blogs.windows.com/windowsexperience/2025/05/19/securing-the-model-context-protocol-building-a-safer-agentic-future-on-windows/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `microsoft2025securing`.

At Microsoft Build 2025, Microsoft previewed its plans for Windows 11 to support MCP as a foundation for agentic computing and said an early private preview would go to developers after Build. Microsoft says MCP client-server traffic will pass through a trusted Windows proxy that centralises policy, consent, authentication and auditing, and that users must approve each client-tool pair. It says only servers meeting baseline requirements will appear in the Windows MCP server registry: code signing, tool definitions that cannot change at runtime, security testing, package identity and declared privileges. Microsoft notes that the private preview may include security controls that are not yet enforced.

- **Relevance:** An OS-level mediating proxy and registry is a concrete model for where policy, consent and audit sit when agent tool access moves between machines and hosts.
- **Operations:** tool-access, identity-trust, governance, observability. **Technologies:** MCP, Windows 11.
- **Source:** official-blog, primary; claim status: vendor-claim; verified by fetch.

### AMN-016

Oligo Security described CVE-2025-49596 (CVSS 9.4), a remote code execution flaw in Anthropic's MCP Inspector developer tool affecting versions below 0.14.1. Because the Inspector client and proxy did not authenticate each other, JavaScript on a malicious web page could send a cross-site request to the proxy on 0.0.0.0:6277 and launch arbitrary stdio commands; a DNS rebinding variant was also shown. Anthropic's fix added a default session token and origin verification.

- **Relevance:** Unauthenticated local proxies are a recurring weak point in MCP tooling, relevant to any design that relocates agents onto developer machines or shared hosts.
- **Operations:** tool-access, identity-trust. **Technologies:** MCP, MCP Inspector.

### AMN-017

JFrog Security Research disclosed CVE-2025-6514 (CVSS 9.6) in mcp-remote, a proxy that lets local MCP clients connect to remote servers, affecting versions 0.0.5 to 0.1.15 and fixed in 0.1.16. A malicious or hijacked server could return a crafted OAuth authorization_endpoint that mcp-remote passed to the OS browser launcher, giving full command execution on Windows and limited executable launch on macOS and Linux. JFrog says this was the first full client-side RCE in a real-world MCP scenario.

- **Relevance:** The OAuth discovery step is where an agent crosses trust boundaries to a new server, and this flaw shows that metadata from the remote side must be validated before any action.

The MCP maintainers launched the official MCP Registry in preview at registry.modelcontextprotocol.io as an open catalog and API for publicly available MCP servers. The registry and its OpenAPI specification are open source so that public marketplaces and private enterprise sub-registries can build on it, and maintainers can denylist servers reported for spam, malicious code or impersonation. The preview carries no durability guarantees and may introduce breaking changes before general availability.

On MCP's first anniversary the maintainers released specification version 2025-11-25. It added experimental Tasks (SEP-1686), so any request can be wrapped in a pollable task with working, input-required, completed, failed and cancelled states, and allowed client registration via OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents (SEP-991). It also added machine-to-machine client credentials (SEP-1046), enterprise IdP controls (SEP-990), URL-mode elicitation (SEP-1036), sampling with tools (SEP-1577) and an extensions framework.

### AMN-069

**The 2026 MCP Roadmap**. David Soria Parra. *Model Context Protocol Blog*, 2026-03-09. <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-mcp-roadmap/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `model20262026`.

MCP lead maintainer David Soria Parra published a 2026 roadmap organised around priority areas instead of release milestones, with Working Groups setting the timelines for their deliverables. The four priorities are: transport scalability (letting Streamable HTTP servers scale horizontally without holding state, plus .well-known metadata so capabilities can be discovered without a live connection); agent communication (retry and expiry semantics for the experimental SEP-1686 Tasks); governance maturation (a contributor ladder, and letting trusted Working Groups accept SEPs in their own domain); and enterprise readiness (audit trails, SSO-integrated auth, gateway behaviour and configuration portability), for which no dedicated Working Group exists yet. The post says no new official transports will be added this cycle and names SEP-1932 (DPoP) and SEP-1933 (Workload Identity Federation) among the proposals in review.

- **Relevance:** Stateless transport, task lifecycle and configuration portability are the protocol changes that most directly determine whether agent work can relocate between hosts.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation, delegation, identity-trust, governance. **Technologies:** MCP, Streamable HTTP, DPoP, Workload Identity Federation.
- **Source:** standards-announcement, primary; claim status: fact; verified by fetch.

### AMN-084

**The AWS MCP Server is now generally available**. Amazon Web Services. *Amazon Web Services*, 2026-05-06. <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/05/aws-mcp-server/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `amazon2026aws`.

### AMN-088

**The 2026-07-28 Specification**. David Soria Parra, Den Delimarsky. *Model Context Protocol Blog*, 2026-07-28. <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `model20262026a`.

MCP's lead maintainers released specification version 2026-07-28. It removes the initialize/initialized handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header, so each request carries its protocol version, client identity and capabilities in _meta, and an optional server/discover call is available. Server-to-client interactions such as elicitation and sampling are reworked as Multi Round-Trip Requests (SEP-2322), Streamable HTTP requests must send Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers (SEP-2243), and list responses carry ttlMs and cacheScope cache hints (SEP-2549). Authorization adds RFC 9207 issuer validation, binds client credentials to the issuing server, and formally deprecates Dynamic Client Registration in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents. Tasks move to an extension (SEP-2663), and Roots, Sampling, Logging and the legacy HTTP+SSE transport are deprecated with at least a twelve-month window.

- **Relevance:** A stateless core means no session needs to be migrated, so an MCP client or server can be relocated or load-balanced between requests, which simplifies runtime relocation.
- **Operations:** runtime-relocation, tool-access, identity-trust, delegation, observability. **Technologies:** MCP, Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0, Client ID Metadata Documents, MCP Apps.
- **Source:** standards-announcement, primary; claim status: fact; verified by fetch. Note: Anthropic's companion post 'Bringing MCP 2026-07-28 to Claude' (same date) claims 400M+ monthly SDK downloads; not included as a separate item to avoid duplicating the event.

### AMN-092

**The New MCP Roadmap**. David Soria Parra, Den Delimarsky. *Model Context Protocol Blog*, 2026-08-22. <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/mcp-roadmap/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `model2026new`.

Following the 2026-07-28 specification release, MCP lead maintainers David Soria Parra and Den Delimarsky published a new roadmap with five priority areas. These are: agentic messaging primitives (server-initiated events, and maturing the Tasks extension SEP-2663 so it can move into the specification); HTTP-native transport unification, extended to local servers speaking Streamable HTTP over stdio; agent identity and enterprise security; improved primitives (one clear tools/call result contract and progressive tool discovery); and SDK developer experience. The identity work includes finalising DPoP and defining an agent identity and delegation path through Workload Identity Federation, the ID-JAG grant and standard token exchange, along with continued engagement with the IETF OAuth and WIMSE working groups.

- **Relevance:** An explicit agent identity and delegation path built on token exchange is the accountability mechanism that delegation and handoff research needs at the tool layer.
- **Operations:** delegation, identity-trust, runtime-relocation, tool-access. **Technologies:** MCP, Streamable HTTP, DPoP, Workload Identity Federation, OAuth token exchange, ID-JAG.
- **Source:** standards-announcement, primary; claim status: fact; verified by fetch.


## T3: Security, identity, authorization and trust

### AMN-015

**Okta introduces Cross App Access to help secure AI agents in the enterprise**. Okta. *Okta*, 2025-06-23. <https://www.okta.com/newsroom/press-releases/okta-introduces-cross-app-access-to-help-secure-ai-agents-in-the/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `okta2025okta`.

Okta announced Cross App Access, a protocol that extends OAuth so that an enterprise identity provider, rather than each user, mediates agent and app-to-app connections. In the described flow the AI tool requests access from Okta, Okta checks enterprise policy and issues a token that the target app validates, with no extra per-user consent prompt. Okta said it would be available to select Okta Platform customers in Q3 2025 and that it was working with ISVs and the MCP and A2A communities.

- **Relevance:** Centralises the policy decision for an agent acting on a user's behalf across applications, which is the authorization step any cross-organization handoff needs.
- **Operations:** identity-trust, delegation, tool-access, governance. **Technologies:** Cross App Access (XAA), OAuth 2.0, MCP, A2A.
- **Source:** press-release, primary; claim status: vendor-claim; verified by fetch.

### AMN-025

**Introducing Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity: Securing agentic AI at scale**. Rahul Sharma, Fei Yuan, Satveer Khurpa, Antonio Rodriguez. *AWS Machine Learning Blog*, 2025-08-15. <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/introducing-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-identity-securing-agentic-ai-at-scale/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `aws2025introducinga`.

AWS described AgentCore Identity, an identity and access service for AI agents in the (then preview) Bedrock AgentCore platform. It comprises an agent identity directory, an agent authorizer for inbound calls (IAM SigV4, OAuth 2.0/OIDC, JWT), a resource credential provider, and a token vault for user OAuth tokens. Agents can call AWS and third-party services such as GitHub, Salesforce and Slack either as themselves (two-legged OAuth) or on behalf of users (three-legged OAuth), with credentials bound to specific agent-user pairs and encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys.

- **Relevance:** Separates the agent's own identity from delegated user credentials, a split that determines what credentials can legitimately travel with a relocated or delegated task.
- **Operations:** identity-trust, delegation, tool-access. **Technologies:** Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT, SigV4, AWS KMS, MCP.
- **Source:** official-blog, primary; claim status: vendor-claim; verified by fetch. Note: The post states AgentCore services were free to try until 16 September 2025 and links to a preview announcement.

### AMN-033

**ForcedLeak: AI agent risks exposed in Salesforce Agentforce**. Sasi Levi. *Noma Security*, 2025-09-25. <https://noma.security/blog/forcedleak-agent-risks-exposed-in-salesforce-agentforce/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `noma2025forcedleak`.

Noma Labs disclosed ForcedLeak, a vulnerability chain rated CVSS 9.4 in Salesforce Agentforce. An attacker hid instructions in the Description field of a Web-to-Lead form; when an employee later asked Agentforce about the lead, the agent followed them and sent CRM data out through image requests to an allowlisted domain that had expired and that the researchers bought for about $5. ### AMN-004

**Agent File**. Letta. *Letta*, 2025-04-02. <https://www.letta.com/blog/agent-file> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `letta2025agent`.

Letta calls it the first file format for portable, reproducible agent state and says it enables moving agents between cloud and local servers, sharing and versioning them. Cloudflare previewed the next Agents SDK, which adds primitives for long-running agents on Durable Objects. runFiber() registers a durable invocation in SQLite before it runs, ctx.stash() saves a checkpoint so an evicted agent resumes from its last stash, and an experimental Session API stores conversations as forkable trees with non-destructive compaction. Sub-agents run as colocated child Durable Objects (Facets), each with an isolated SQLite database, and talk to the parent over typed RPC.

He presents Stacklok's recently open-sourced, still-early Mecatl runtime, which separates the core agent loop from clients, execution environments and tools. The OpenID Foundation's Artificial Intelligence Identity Management Community Group published the whitepaper 'Identity Management for Agentic AI'. It concludes that current identity standards work for simpler agents operating within one organization or accessing a user's own data. It also finds that they were not designed for recursive delegation chains or cross-domain trust propagation and will struggle with the scale of authorization decisions made by autonomous agents. It recommends that enterprises treat agents as first-class identities with lifecycle management, governance and accountability, and that standards bodies develop agent identity and delegation protocols.

- **Relevance:** Recursive delegation and cross-domain trust propagation are exactly the identity problems raised when a task is handed across agents and organizations.

## T7: Agent-to-user, agentic commerce and cross-organization action

### AMN-007

**Mastercard unveils Agent Pay, pioneering agentic payments technology to power commerce in the age of AI**. Mastercard. *Mastercard*, 2025-04-29. <https://newsroom.mastercard.com/news/press/2025/april/mastercard-unveils-agent-pay-pioneering-agentic-payments-technology-to-power-commerce-in-the-age-of-ai> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `mastercard2025mastercard`.

Mastercard unveiled Agent Pay, which centres on Agentic Tokens that build on the tokenisation it already uses for contactless, card-on-file, Payment Passkeys and programmable payments. Mastercard says AI agents must be registered and verified before they can pay for users, that consumers control what an agent may buy on their behalf, and that participants across the payment chain, including merchants and issuers, will be able to recognise agent-initiated transactions. It names Microsoft (Azure OpenAI Service and Copilot Studio), IBM watsonx Orchestrate, Braintree and Checkout.com as collaborators. Its chief product officer says the company wants to work on standards such as applying the Model Context Protocol to Secure Remote Commerce.

- **Relevance:** Binds a delegated payment credential to a registered agent identity with user-set limits, an early network-level pattern for accountable delegation.
- **Operations:** identity-trust, delegation. **Technologies:** Mastercard Agent Pay, Agentic Tokens, MCP, Microsoft Copilot Studio, IBM watsonx Orchestrate.

### AMN-010

**Introducing AG-UI: The Protocol Where Agents Meet Users**. Nathan Tarbert. *CopilotKit*, 2025-05-12. <https://www.copilotkit.ai/blog/introducing-ag-ui-the-protocol-where-agents-meet-users> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `copilotkit2025introducing`.

CopilotKit announced AG-UI, an open Agent-User Interaction Protocol. A client sends one POST to an agent endpoint and then listens to a single stream of JSON events over plain HTTP or an optional binary channel. Example events include text message content, tool-call starts, state deltas and lifecycle signals, and TypeScript and Python SDKs are available. CopilotKit says frameworks such as LangChain, CrewAI, Mastra and AG2 each speak different dialects, and presents AG-UI as a consistent contract between agents and interfaces so UIs no longer need custom adapters.

- **Relevance:** Defines a framework-neutral event and shared-state stream between agent and user, a candidate carrier for task state and human approval when work moves between agent backends.
- **Operations:** delegation, portable-context, cross-framework-migration. **Technologies:** AG-UI, CopilotKit, LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, AG2.
- **Source:** official-blog, primary; claim status: vendor-claim; verified by fetch.

### AMN-024

**Perplexity is using stealth, undeclared crawlers to evade website no-crawl directives**. Gabriel Corral, Vaibhav Singhal, Brian Mitchell, Reid Tatoris. *Cloudflare Blog*, 2025-08-04. <https://blog.cloudflare.com/perplexity-is-using-stealth-undeclared-crawlers-to-evade-website-no-crawl-directives/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `cloudflare2025perplexity`.

Cloudflare reports that after customers blocked Perplexity's declared crawlers (PerplexityBot and Perplexity-User), Perplexity appeared to switch to an undeclared crawler with a generic Chrome-on-macOS user agent. Cloudflare says this crawler rotated through IP addresses outside Perplexity's published ranges and sent requests from different ASNs, across tens of thousands of domains and millions of daily requests. In response, Cloudflare says it de-listed Perplexity as a verified bot and added signatures for the crawler to its managed blocking rule. It contrasts this with OpenAI: in its tests, OpenAI's crawler stopped when robots.txt disallowed it or a block page appeared, and Cloudflare says ChatGPT Agent signs its HTTP requests with Web Bot Auth.

- **Relevance:** Shows the dispute over whether a user-directed agent must identify itself to the sites it acts on, which motivated signed-agent schemes.
- **Operations:** identity-trust, governance. **Technologies:** Web Bot Auth, robots.txt, Perplexity, ChatGPT Agent, bot management.
- **Source:** research-news, primary; claim status: incident; verified by fetch. Note: Page metadata also shows a later modification date (2026-07-15). Perplexity's rebuttal not fetched.

### AMN-026

**Agentic Browser Security: Indirect Prompt Injection in Perplexity Comet**. Artem Chaikin, Shivan Kaul Sahib. *Brave*, 2025-08-20. <https://brave.com/blog/comet-prompt-injection/> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `brave2025agentic`.

Brave disclosed that Perplexity's Comet browser passed webpage content to its LLM without separating it from user instructions. In a demonstration, a hidden Reddit comment made the agent extract the user's Perplexity account email address and read a one-time password from Gmail and exfiltrate them, which enabled account takeover without further user input. Brave reported the flaw on 25 July 2025, found Perplexity's fixes incomplete, and recommended isolating agentic browsing, checking that actions match the user's intent, and requiring explicit confirmation for sensitive actions.

- **Relevance:** Shows that an agent acting with a user's full authenticated privileges across sites breaks same-origin assumptions, so delegated cross-organisation actions need confirmation and isolation.
- **Operations:** identity-trust, governance. **Technologies:** Perplexity Comet, agentic browser, prompt injection.
- **Source:** research-news, primary; claim status: incident; verified by fetch.

### AMN-027

**Piloting Claude in Chrome**. Anthropic (claude.com blog). *Anthropic (claude.com blog)*, 2025-08-25. <https://claude.com/blog/claude-for-chrome> (accessed 2026-10-15). Cite key: `anthropic2025piloting`.

Anthropic opened a research preview of a Chrome-extension browser agent to 1,000 Max-plan users. In red-teaming of 123 cases across 29 attack scenarios, Anthropic reports that the attack success rate fell from 23.6% to 11.2% with new mitigations, and from 35.7% to 0% on a four-type browser-specific challenge set. Users grant or revoke access per site, Claude asks for confirmation before high-risk actions such as purchasing or publishing, and some site categories are blocked. Later updates widened availability (Max beta in November 2025; Pro/Team/Enterprise in December 2025).

- **Relevance:** Gives quantified evidence that human-in-the-loop confirmation and per-site permissions are still needed when an agent acts on third-party sites.
- **Operations:** governance, identity-trust. **Technologies:** Claude in Chrome, browser agent, prompt injection.

Cloudflare announced it would form the x402 Foundation with Coinbase to steward x402, the protocol that revives HTTP 402 Payment Required for machine-to-machine payments. ### AMN-058

Google made the A2UI project public with its format at v0.8. A2UI is an Apache 2-licensed open-source effort in which agents describe user interfaces as declarative data instead of executable code, and the client renders them from its own catalogue of trusted native components. Early client libraries cover Flutter, Web Components (Lit) and Angular. Google says A2UI payloads can travel over A2A or AG UI, that the AG UI/CopilotKit team worked with it on day-zero compatibility, that Flutter's GenUI SDK already uses A2UI, and that A2UI is being integrated into Gemini Enterprise.

- **Relevance:** Lets a remote (possibly cross-organisation) agent in a delegation chain request user input without shipping code into the host, which matters for safety when tasks are handed between agents.

### AMN-089

A three-judge Ninth Circuit panel vacated the March 2026 preliminary injunction against Perplexity's Comet browser. The panel found Amazon unlikely to succeed on its CFAA and California claims because, on the current record, Perplexity itself did not access Amazon's systems and the assistant acted as a tool on the user's instructions. The panel said the ruling is limited to the existing record and sets no broad rule on agentic AI. The case returns to the district court.
